extracted.intended_audience: graduate students / advanced undergraduates studying category theory and homological algebra (readers learning abelian categories and diagram lemmas)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, characterizations, and basic lemmas for additive and abelian categories, exact and left-exact functors, diagram-chasing techniques (members), the snake/five lemmas, and filtered limits/colimits. Intended as textbook material for learning and applying these concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additive functor (basic equation)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additive functor T: A -> B (where A and B are Ab-categories) satisfies T(f + f') = T f + T f' for any parallel pair of arrows f, f': a -> b in A. It follows that T(0) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the defining algebraic condition for a functor between Ab-categories to be additive; it may be checked on pairs of parallel morphisms. Equivalent formulations (below) are often easier to verify in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additive functor preserves biproducts
rubrics_metrics.description: If A and B are Ab-categories and A has all binary biproducts, then a functor T: A -> B is additive if and only if T carries each binary biproduct diagram in A to a biproduct diagram in B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checking that T preserves the universal biproduct equations (P_i i_j = δ_ij, i_1 P_1 + i_2 P_2 = 1) suffices to conclude additivity. Variants: T is additive iff it preserves binary products, or iff it preserves binary coproducts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of additive functors
rubrics_metrics.description: Hom-functors A(a,-) and A(-,a) (when hom-sets are small), projections from A x B to factors, tensor product Ab x Ab -> Ab, and torsion product are additive (tensor and torsion product are additive in each argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are standard examples to test intuition and to use as building blocks; when verifying additivity check termwise or factorwise behavior on sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additive category (alternative construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a category has a null object, finite products and finite coproducts, and the canonical arrow from a coproduct to the corresponding product is always an isomorphism, then defining f + f' via the composite through the product/coproduct gives each hom-set the structure of a commutative monoid and composition distributes; with further existence of inverses one gets an additive category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This alternative route (exercise) constructs addition from biproduct data; it recovers the usual notion of additive category (Mac Lane [1950]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of abelian category (axioms)
rubrics_metrics.description: An abelian category A is an Ab-category satisfying (i) A has a null object, (ii) A has binary biproducts, (iii) every arrow in A has a kernel and a cokernel, (iv) every monic arrow is a kernel and every epi is a cokernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four conditions together ensure the usual homological algebra machinery (images, coimages, exact sequences, finite limits/colimits) works in A. Variants: (i) can be replaced by initial/terminal object, (ii) by binary products or coproducts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of abelian axioms: finite limits/colimits
rubrics_metrics.description: With existence of kernels (iii) and the null object and biproducts (i,ii), A has all finite limits; dually, cokernels give all finite colimits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use kernels and products/equalizers (and dually cokernels and coproducts/coequalizers) to construct finite limits/colimits in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monic+epi implies iso (abelian)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an abelian category, any arrow that is both monic and epi is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from (iv): monic = kernel of some map, combined with epi cancels to show the kernel is identity; use in proofs to deduce isomorphisms from two-sided cancellability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functor category AJ is abelian
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is abelian and J is any category, then the functor category A^J is abelian: Nat(S,T) is an abelian group with termwise addition, null functor is null object, biproducts and kernels are defined termwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a large supply of abelian categories and justifies doing homological algebra 'pointwise' on diagrams/functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monic–epi factorization and image/coimage
rubrics_metrics.description: In an abelian category every arrow f factors f = m e with m monic and e epi; moreover m = ker(coker f) and e = coker(ker f). Any other monic–epi factorization is uniquely isomorphic to this one. Define image = im f = m and coimage = coim f = e (unique up to iso).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This canonical factorization is functorial and underlies definition of images/coimages; in concrete categories (Ab, R-Mod) it recovers the usual quotient/inclusion with an isomorphism between coimage and image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness at a point (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A composable pair a --f--> b --g--> c is exact at b when im f ≅ ker g (equivalently coker f ≅ coim g). Equivalently, gf = 0, and every member killed by g lies in the image of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bipartite definition mirrors the elementwise notion in Ab and is the basis for short exact sequences and homological constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short exact sequence (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence 0 -> a --f--> b --g--> c -> 0 is exact at a, b, and c; equivalently f = ker g and g = coker f (so f is monic and g is epi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize short exact sequences by the kernel/cokernel conditions (6) given in the text; used pervasively in homological algebra and Ext descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact / left exact functor (definitions & characterizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A functor T: A -> B between abelian categories is exact if it preserves all finite limits and all finite colimits. Equivalently, T is additive and preserves kernels and cokernels, hence images/coimages and exact sequences. T is left exact if it preserves all finite limits (equivalently T additive and ker(T f) = T(ker f) for all f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To check exactness often verify additivity and preservation of kernels and cokernels (or check preservation of short exact sequences). Left-exactness can be checked on kernels/short left exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economical formulation of abelian category (without given hom-group structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category A satisfying (i) null object, (ii') binary products and binary coproducts, (iii) every arrow has kernel and cokernel, (iv) every monic is kernel and every epi is cokernel, can be endowed with addition on hom-sets via formula (2.6) to become abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows abelian structure can be recovered from limits/colimits and kernel/cokernel data; references Freyd/Schubert for full proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain complex in an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: A chain complex in an abelian category A is a sequence ... -> C_{n+1} -> C_n -> C_{n-1} -> ... with composition d_n d_{n+1} = 0 for all n. Homology objects are defined as usual H_n = ker d_n / im d_{n+1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All homological constructions (homology, long exact sequences) make sense in any abelian category; diagram lemmas for complexes are proved using categorical methods analogous to element-chasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of short exact sequences (Ses A)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of short exact sequences is a triple (f,g,h) of arrows making the obvious diagram commute; the collection of short exact sequences with these morphisms forms a category Ses A which is additive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This organizes exact sequences into an additive category and is used in defining bifunctors like Ext and naturality statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short Five Lemma (diagram criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a commutative diagram with short exact rows, if f and h are monic then g is monic; dually if f and h are epi then g is epi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the categorical (element-free) version used in diagram chases via 'members'; use kernel arguments rather than elements in abelian categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback preserves epis in abelian categories (and kernel factorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a pullback square in an abelian category, if the right vertical arrow f is epi then the left vertical arrow f' is epi. Moreover, the kernel k of f factors as k = g' k' with k' the kernel of f'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that pullbacks are constructed from products and equalizers; this fact is essential when pulling back short exact sequences to produce new short exact sequences (used in Ext constructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Members and equivalence relation for diagram chasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a 'member' x with codomain a to be any arrow x: ? -> a; define x == y if there exist epis u,v with x u = y v. Members form equivalence classes which play the role of 'elements' in diagram chases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'members' formalism lets one perform element-style diagram chasing in arbitrary abelian categories; it yields elementary rules replacing element arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary rules for chasing diagrams (Theorem 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of categorical analogues of elementwise rules: (i) f monic iff for all x in a, f x == 0 implies x == 0; (ii) f monic iff f x == f x' implies x == x'; (iii) g epi iff for each z in c there exists y in b with g y == z; (iv) h is zero iff for all x in r, h x = 0; (v) exactness at b iff g f = 0 and every y with g y = 0 is f x for some x; (vi) subtraction rule: if g x = g y then there exists z with g z = 0 and relations capturing differences and compatibilities with other maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules replace elementwise manipulations; they are used repeatedly in diagram chases like proofs of the five lemma, snake lemma, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Lemma (criterion for isomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a commutative diagram with exact rows b1->b2->b3->b4->b5 and corresponding rows, if f1, f2, f4, f5 are isomorphisms then f3 is an isomorphism (proved by showing f3 is monic and epi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use members-based diagram-chasing rules to prove monicity and epi-ness for f3; a standard tool for deducing middle isomorphism from outer isomorphisms in exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ker–coker (Snake) sequence existence and exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a morphism (f,g,h) of short exact sequences, there exists a connecting morphism b: Ker h -> Coker f such that the long sequence 0 -> Ker f -> Ker g -> Ker h --b--> Coker f -> Coker g -> Coker h -> 0 is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The snake lemma construction is given by a pullback/pushout zig-zag and the connecting morphism can be described by a staircase; exactness is proved by members-based chasing. This is the standard tool to get long exact sequences of kernels/cokernels and underlies connecting morphisms in homology/derived functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of filtered category (directedness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category J is filtered when J is nonempty and (a) for any two objects j,j' there exists k with arrows j->k and j'->k, and (b) for any two parallel arrows u,v: i->j there exists w: j->k with w u = w v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filtered categories generalize directed preorders; finite diagrams in a filtered category always admit a cocone. This is the categorical notion used to define filtered colimits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered colimit (definition and construction principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: A filtered colimit is a colimit over a filtered category J. Important facts: categories with finite coproducts and colimits over all small directed preorders have all small coproducts (Theorem 1). The forgetful functor Grp -> Set creates filtered colimits, so filtered colimits in Grp are computed on underlying sets with unique induced group structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use filtered colimits to build large coproducts via directed systems of finite coproducts. For algebraic categories (Alg_r), the underlying-set colimit can be equipped with the unique algebra structure making structure maps homomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interchange of colimits (Fubini-type formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a bifunctor F: P x J -> X with X cocomplete, the colimits interchange: Colim_p Colim_j F(p,j) ≅ Colim_j Colim_p F(p,j) (under appropriate smallness/cocompleteness hypotheses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interchange allows computing iterated colimits in either order; useful when one variable's colimit is filtered or when applying 'colimit over p then over j' manipulations in proofs.
